title: Woven cotton dishcloth in plain weave
subtitle: A practical 8-shaft rigid heddle or floor loom project in cotton rag yarn
excerpt: Plain-weave dishcloths in cotton warp and weft are one of the fastest practical weaving projects on either a rigid heddle or floor loom. The finished cloth is about 30 cm square, hard-wearing, and improves in absorbency with washing.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional plain-weave cloth practice. Cotton dishcloths are one of the oldest and most universal plain-weave projects; the specific setup described here follows standard rigid heddle guild workshop guidance.

glossaryTerms.definition: The simplest weave structure, where each weft thread passes over one warp thread and under the next, alternating on each row.

items.name: 8/2 cotton yarn for warp and weft, in one or two colours
Rigid heddle loom (at least 30 cm weaving width)
5 dent or 6 dent heddle (5 to 6 threads per cm)

content.text: Wind a warp of 150 threads at 5 threads per cm for a 30 cm finished width (accounting for about 10 per cent draw-in). Cut the warp to 90 cm to allow for loom waste and fringe, allowing for a finished 30 cm cloth with a few extra centimetres for hemstitching. Thread the heddle: alternate threads through the slots and holes as usual for plain weave.

Weave 6 to 8 picks with a waste yarn at the start to space the warp evenly, then hemstitch the weft edge before beginning the cloth proper. Weave at an even beat to keep the weft rows parallel. For a dishcloth, the beat should be firm but not packing: if the weft covers the warp completely, the sett is too open and the cloth will not be balanced. Aim for equal warp and weft visibility on the surface.

Hemstitch the end of the cloth before cutting off. Allow 4 to 5 cm of warp fringe at each end, knot the fringe in pairs or small groups, and trim evenly. Machine wash at 60°C for the first wash to pre-shrink the cloth and set the weave. The cloth will shrink about 10 per cent in length and width on the first wash; subsequent washes shrink it less. Air dry flat.

items.problem: The cloth is drawing in significantly at the selvedges
items.cause: The weft is being pulled too tightly as it is beaten in, narrowing the cloth
items.fix: Lay the weft in at a wider angle before beating: a 45-degree arc is standard. Also check that the shuttle is passing through the shed without catching the selvedge threads.

items.problem: The warp and weft are not showing equally (warp-dominant or weft-dominant cloth)
items.cause: The sett or beat is unbalanced: either too many or too few warp threads per centimetre for the yarn and beat being used
items.fix: Test with a short sample: weave 5 cm and wet-finish it. Check the balance. Adjust the beat density before weaving the full cloth.
